summary.text: Mantle convection is the very slow creep of Earth's solid mantle as convection currents carry heat from the interior to the surface.
It makes tectonic plates move: hot material rises beneath spreading centres, while cooled, dense plate edges sink back down in subduction.
Plates move at a few centimetres a year, and one shallow convection cycle takes on the order of 50 million years.

items.prompt: The mantle beneath your feet is solid rock. How can it still carry heat by convection?

options.label: It is really a vast ocean of liquid magma
The solid rock creeps very slowly over time
Heat crosses it only as light
It melts and refreezes every year

items.explain: Mantle convection is the very slow creep of the solid mantle as currents carry heat toward the surface.

items.prompt: An ocean plate has travelled far from the ridge where it formed. Why does it eventually sink back into the mantle at a trench?

options.label: The weight of seawater pushes it down
It melts and drips away from the surface
It has cooled and become dense enough to sink
The Moon's pull drags it downward

items.explain: Material cools as it moves away from spreading centres; by the plate's consuming edge it has contracted and become dense, so it sinks under its own weight.

items.prompt: Tectonic plate motion is the surface face of mantle convection. Roughly how fast do the plates move?

options.label: A few metres per year
A few kilometres per year
A few metres per day
A few centimetres per year

items.explain: On a global scale, convection shows up at the surface as plate motions with speeds of a few centimetres per year.

items.prompt: Helium-3 is not made naturally on Earth and quickly escapes once erupted. Why do some lavas rich in it point to a special source?

options.label: Their source was never melted and recycled like ridge rock
Heat near the core keeps making fresh helium-3
The lava soaked up helium-3 from the air
Seawater turns into helium-3 when it hits lava

items.explain: A high helium-3 to helium-4 ratio suggests a source that has not previously been melted the way mid-ocean ridge basalt sources have, interpreted as a less well-mixed region, suggested to be the lower mantle.

items.prompt: In the whole-mantle model of convection, what happens to cold ocean plates that sink at subduction zones?

options.label: They stop about 100 km down
They melt into the liquid outer core
They descend to the core–mantle boundary
They spread out just under the crust

items.explain: In whole mantle convection, cold subducting lithosphere descends from the surface all the way to the core–mantle boundary, while hot plumes rise from there to the surface.

items.prompt: Plates are currently converging toward the western Pacific and the Americas. What is the deep mantle most likely doing beneath those regions?

options.label: Rising in a broad upwelling
Sinking in a broad downwelling
Standing completely still
Melting into one large magma pool

items.explain: Whole mantle convection is thought to include broad downwelling beneath the Americas and the western Pacific, matching plate convergence toward those regions.
